description: Parsing `cmux list-workspaces` output (run with CMUX_QUIET=1) into rows of ref, title and selected. One row per line that starts (after an optional leading `*` and whitespace) with a workspace ref: `workspace:N` with a non-empty N, or a bare UUID. The selected row is marked by a leading `*` in column 0, a trailing `[selected]` tag, or both, because cmux changed its format once and both must keep working. Only the trailing tag counts, never `[selected]` elsewhere in a title, and if several rows claim selection while a `*` row exists, the `*` row wins. The title is the rest of the line with one leading status glyph stripped (see status-glyph.json). Anything else (blank lines, the legacy-alias notice, headers, other object kinds) is skipped. Lines are split on LF only; cmux on macOS never emits CRLF. A wrong parse sends dictated text into a workspace the person never chose.
function: RemoteControlService.parseWorkspaces(_:) — raw stdout string in, ordered list of {ref, title, selected} out
verifiedBy: Characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #93, ticket #121); Tests/PowerUpTests/CmuxReportingFixtureTests.swift. The documented sample row and both selection markers come from live `cmux list-workspaces` output recorded in DESIGN.md (remote-control addendum).
capturedAgainst: cmux 0.64.17 (97) [9ed29d81a] (`cmux --version`, /Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/bin/cmux, 2026-10-23); PowerUp macOS app, branch stage-1-text-views-spikes, 2026-10-23

cases.name: empty output
cases.reason: No workspaces open: the parser must return nothing (the caller then explains), never a phantom row.

cases.name: blank lines only
cases.reason: Whitespace-only output must not produce rows.

cases.name: documented sample: both markers on the selected row
cases.input:
* workspace:11  ⠐ Build PS5 controller voice app  [selected]
  workspace:7   ✳ Design the WeChat mini program
cases.reason: The format recorded in DESIGN.md: leading * and trailing [selected] together; status glyphs stripped from both titles.

cases.name: leading * marker alone
cases.input:
workspace:3  Alpha
* workspace:4  Beta
  workspace:5  Gamma
cases.reason: cmux has printed the selection as only a leading *; auto-targeting must still find it.

cases.name: trailing [selected] marker alone
cases.input:
workspace:3  Alpha
  workspace:4  Beta  [selected]
  workspace:5  Gamma
cases.reason: cmux has printed the selection as only a trailing [selected] tag (the format changed once); both markers must keep working.

cases.name: * with no space before the ref
cases.reason: The star is a column-0 marker, not a separate token; it must be recognised without a following space.

cases.name: [selected] glued to the title
cases.reason: The tag is matched as a suffix of the line, so it is honoured even without a separating space.

cases.name: name containing [selected] mid-title is not selected
cases.input:
* workspace:1  Main
  workspace:2  Fix the [selected] filter bug
cases.reason: A title that merely mentions [selected] must not steal auto-targeting and route input into a workspace the user never chose.

cases.name: name ending in [selected] on the selected row keeps its literal
cases.reason: Only the one trailing tag is removed; the user's own literal stays in the title.

cases.name: name ending in [selected] loses to the * row
cases.reason: When a title ends in the tag text, the leading * is authoritative and the impostor row is demoted. (Its title loses the literal: cosmetic only, targeting uses ref.)

cases.name: name containing * is not selected
cases.input:
workspace:5  fix * in glob
* workspace:6  Main
cases.reason: A * inside a title is not the column-0 selection marker.

cases.name: name starting with * is not selected
cases.reason: The marker is only recognised before the ref, never at the start of a title.

cases.name: case-sensitive [SELECTED] is part of the title
cases.reason: Only cmux's exact lowercase tag marks selection.

cases.name: trailing whitespace after the tag
cases.reason: Padding after the tag or title must neither hide the tag nor leak into the title.

cases.name: trailing newline and wide column padding
cases.reason: cmux aligns columns with runs of spaces; the title starts at the first non-space.

cases.name: legacy-alias notice is skipped
cases.input:
cmux: 'list-workspaces' is now an alias for 'workspace list'
* workspace:1  Main
cases.reason: Without CMUX_QUIET cmux prints a notice line first; it must not become a workspace.

cases.name: rows that are not workspace refs are skipped
cases.input:
Workspaces:
  window:1  Main window
  workspace:  empty ref
* workspace:2  Real
cases.reason: Headers, other object kinds and a bare 'workspace:' are not targets; skipping beats guessing.

cases.name: ref with no title
cases.reason: An untitled workspace is still a target; its picker label falls back to the short ref.

cases.name: UUID refs from --id-format uuids
cases.reason: With uuid ids cmux prints bare UUIDs instead of workspace:N; both letter cases parse.

cases.name: glyph without a following space
cases.reason: cmux sometimes prints the activity glyph glued to the title.

cases.name: emoji title and ellipsis title survive parsing
cases.reason: Only the status glyph is stripped: the user's emoji and cmux's truncation ellipsis stay, so the title is recognisable.

cases.name: CJK title
cases.reason: Non-Latin titles pass through intact after the glyph.

cases.name: two * rows are both selected
cases.reason: The parser reports what cmux printed; the auto-target picks the first selected row.

cases.name: two [selected] rows without any * are both selected
cases.reason: Demotion only happens when a * row exists to be authoritative; otherwise the auto-target picks the first.

cases.name: no marker at all
cases.reason: Nothing is invented as selected; the auto-target then falls back to the first row.

cases.name: CRLF output is one line
cases.reason: Lines are split on the LF character only; CR LF is one character that is not LF, so CRLF output (which cmux on macOS never prints) is one row whose title carries the rest. Pinned so every implementation splits alike.

cases.name: a tab does not separate the ref from the title
cases.reason: Only a space separates the ref; a tab stays inside the ref token (workspace: plus a non-empty rest is still a ref), so the title is empty rather than guessed.

cases.name: a non-numeric workspace ref is accepted
cases.reason: Any non-empty text after workspace: is a ref; the number is not checked, so a future ref spelling keeps working.

cases.name: uppercase WORKSPACE: is not a ref
cases.reason: The workspace: prefix is case-sensitive; anything else is skipped, never guessed.

cases.name: malformed UUIDs are skipped
cases.reason: A bare ref must be the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form of ASCII hex digits, as Foundation's UUID(uuidString:) accepts it: braces, a missing hyphen, a non-hex or full-width digit and a short form are not refs.

cases.name: a NUL ends the UUID check
cases.reason: Foundation reads the token as a C string, so a UUID followed by a NUL and more text is accepted with the whole token as the ref; every implementation must accept the same refs.

cases.name: a lone star or tag is skipped
cases.reason: A line that is only selection markers has no ref and is skipped, so it can never steal the selection.

cases.name: a combining mark on the star is not the marker
cases.reason: The star must be a character of its own; a star a combining mark extends is not a marker, and the token it starts is not a ref.

cases.name: a combining mark on the tag hides it
cases.reason: The tag must end the line as whole characters; a combining mark on its bracket makes it part of the title, not a selection.

cases.name: no-break space after the star is trimmed
cases.reason: After the star the line is trimmed of spaces and tabs (no-break space included), but only an ordinary space separates the ref, so the no-break space after the ref stays in it.

cases.name: a line separator after the star is not trimmed
cases.reason: After the star only spaces and tabs are trimmed, not line separators, so the token does not start with workspace: and the row is skipped.

cases.name: a zero-width space after the star is trimmed
cases.reason: Foundation's whitespace set includes U+200B, so it is trimmed after the star like a space.

cases.name: duplicate refs are both kept
cases.reason: Rows are reported as listed, never merged or deduplicated.
